verdict.reasoning: Patient states shortness of breath started over the last hour while sitting watching TV: "over the last hour, I've started to feel, like, a bit short of breath" and confirmed it was while "sitting watching tv."
Same as cc-001: onset over the last hour and occurred while she was "sitting watching tv," indicating sudden/acute onset while seated.

Patient describes feeling her heart racing along with shortness of breath: "I feel like I'm getting really stressed out because, like, my heart is really going." and doctor clarifies, "you're feeling your heart more than normal?" "Yeah." This supports palpitations accompanying SOB.
When asked about chest pain: "And the shortness of breath, does it cause any pain in your chest?" patient replies "No."
On deep breath: "How about when you take a very deep breath in?" Patient: "I mean, yeah, my chest feels sore, but so does my C section scar." This supports chest soreness on deep inspiration.

Patient reports a cough starting yesterday and not bringing anything up: "So I started with a cough yesterday." and later, "Have you brought anything up?" "No, I haven't. No." This supports a non-productive cough beginning yesterday.
Patient notes tenderness including at the C-section scar: "my chest feels sore, but so does my C section scar. You know, it's all tender."
Patient: "I had a C section a few weeks ago." Clarified: "Yeah. Four weeks."

Regarding codeine: "They gave me some codeine." and "Yeah, I've been taking that fairly regularly, but probably haven't taken it for a week." This supports postoperative codeine use with last dose about a week ago.
Allergy: "I'm allergic to ibuprofen, though." When asked what happens, she says, "I don't know." This matches allergy to ibuprofen with unspecified reaction.
Family history: "my mum's had clots in her legs before."

Transcript only states: "Is anyone else with you at home?" "No, my partner's at work." This indicates partner is usually present but currently at work; it does not confirm that the patient lives with her partner. Claim that she lives with her partner adds unspoken living arrangement details.
She had a C-section four weeks ago and is with baby: "And are you with baby at the moment?" "Yes, I am." and C-section timing "Four weeks." This supports caring for a roughly four-week-old baby.
After counting pulse: "How many did you count?" "I counted 30." This was over a brief timed count, consistent with self-palpated 30 beats.
Clinician interprets pulse: "Good. So your heart is running slightly fast at the moment."

Transcript includes only pulse count and description of rate; no other vitals (e.g., BP, RR, O2 sat, temp) or formal physical exam findings are documented. Stating that none were provided is consistent with the absence of such data.

Clinician links acute postpartum SOB and clot risk in lungs (possible PE): "Given that you've had a C section and you're short of breath, which has come on quite recently and quite quickly..." and later, "some people can suffer with clots, and those can either be found in the legs or... your chest. So in your lungs." This supports concern for pulmonary embolism as part of assessment.
The recent cough is part of the clinical picture: "So I started with a cough yesterday." and further questioning about it. Including it as an assessment item matches how it was handled.

Post-C-section pain/tenderness discussed: "my chest feels sore, but so does my C section scar. You know, it's all tender." and advice not to take codeine "if you're taking any medications, like codeine, don't take them..." It is reasonable that post-C-section pain is considered in assessment.

ED evaluation and self-transport: "it might be worth you going into the hospital to get checked out a bit further." and options: "I can call an ambulance or you can take yourself to the hospital with baby." Patient: "I'll go. I'll take myself."
Medication advice: "And if you're taking any medications, like codeine, don't take them for the time being."

Clinician explains clot risk and that if a clot is found they can give something to reduce it: "if that does become the case, they can give you something to reduce the clot." However, there is no explicit discussion of specific ED plan for imaging or anticoagulation. Mention of imaging and anticoagulation is added detail not in transcript.

Transport options: "I can call an ambulance or you can take yourself to the hospital with baby. Which one would you prefer?" Patient: "It feels a bit dramatic to call an ambulance. I'll go. I'll take myself." This shows ambulance was offered and declined.

Transcript does not mention explicit safety-net advice about symptoms worsening en route or contingency if her partner is unavailable. Only states partner is at work and to go to hospital quickly with baby. The detailed safety-net statement is not present.
